payload.name: gammatone-filter
payload.scope: A human-made linear filter whose impulse response is an exponentially-modulated sinusoid (a gamma-shaped envelope), realized as a cascade of resonator sections to model the frequency selectivity of the auditory periphery; the dynamic counterpart to the static triangular mel-filter-bank.

payload.body: A gammatone-filter is a human-made linear time-invariant filter whose impulse response is an exponentially-modulated sinusoid — a gamma-shaped envelope h(t)=t^n·e^(−αt)·cos(2πf_c·t + φ) for t≥0 — that models the frequency selectivity of the auditory periphery. It is typically realized as a cascade of four second-order resonator (complex-pole) sections, each tuned to a center frequency f_c, where the decay rate α and the resonance Q set the bandwidth (commonly mapped to the equivalent rectangular bandwidth, ERB). Parameters: (1) center frequency f_c; (2) bandwidth/selectivity (ERB or Q), which sets the decay rate α and the resonator pole placement; (3) the envelope order n and the modulation phase φ; (4) the number of cascade sections (classically four). Persistence mechanism: it persists as a standard mathematical model — the closed-form impulse response plus the resonator-section difference equations — carried in auditory-modeling and audio-analysis literature (the classic gammatone and gammatone-filter-bank toolkits in MATLAB/Python, e.g. the Cochlea and gammatone libraries) and reused as a transform in cochlear and speech-processing front-ends. Boundary: it is a dynamic, time-domain resonator whose output is a decaying oscillation, not the static triangular mel-filter-bank that multiplies a power spectrum by fixed mel-spaced weights. [formal: resonantia gamma-soni | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

payload.name: equivalent-rectangular-bandwidth
payload.scope: A human-made, frequency-dependent unit of filter bandwidth (the ERB) that describes the frequency selectivity of the auditory periphery; the bandwidth of a flat rectangular filter that would pass the same energy as a given auditory filter. The standard psychophysical unit used to set the spacing and width of gammatone, bark, and auditory-filter-bank filters.

payload.name: equivalent-rectangular-bandwidth
payload.scope: A human-made, frequency-dependent unit of filter bandwidth (the ERB) that describes the frequency selectivity of the auditory periphery; the bandwidth of a flat rectangular filter that would pass the same energy as a given auditory filter. The standard psychophysical unit used to set the spacing and width of gammatone, bark, and auditory-filter-bank filters.

payload.body: An equivalent-rectangular-bandwidth (ERB) is a human-made, frequency-dependent unit of filter bandwidth used to describe the frequency selectivity of the auditory periphery. It is defined as the width of a rectangular (flat) bandpass filter that would pass the same energy as a given auditory filter centered at frequency f. The standard empirical expression is ERB(f) = 24.7·(4.37·f + 1), with f in kHz and the result in Hz, so the equivalent width is about 104 Hz near 0.1 kHz and grows toward roughly 100·f at high frequencies — the auditory filter narrows relative to its center as f rises. Parameters: (1) the center frequency f (kHz); (2) the chosen fitting curve — the Glasberg & Moore (1990) expression is canonical, with alternative fits in the literature. Persistence mechanism: it persists as a standard psychophysically derived formula carried in the audiology and auditory-modeling literature (Glasberg & Moore 1990; Moore's auditory-filter and loudness work) and applied operationally to set the spacing and bandwidth of gammatone, bark, and auditory-filter-bank filters. Boundary: it is a unit of measure — a single number in Hz attached to a center frequency — not the auditory filter itself, not a signal's spectral bandwidth, and distinct from the generic signal-processing 'bandwidth' entry. [formal: latitudo rectanguli aequivalens | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

payload.name: auditory-filter
payload.scope: A human-made linear bandpass filter whose center frequency and (ERB) bandwidth match the frequency selectivity of the auditory periphery at that frequency; the general construct instantiated by the gammatone-filter and approximated by the mel- and bark-filter-banks. It is the cochlear analysis filter, not the auditory filter bank that arrays them.

payload.body: An auditory-filter is a human-made linear bandpass filter whose center frequency and bandwidth are chosen to match the frequency selectivity of the auditory periphery at that frequency, so that it approximates the response of a single cochlear channel. The standard parameterization sets the bandwidth to the equivalent-rectangular-bandwidth ERB(f)=24.7·(4.37·f+1) at center f (kHz), with the filter shape given by a gamma-shaped (exponentially-modulated sinusoid) or Lorentzian (ROEX) impulse response. Parameters: (1) center frequency f; (2) the selectivity/bandwidth rule (ERB, or a constant-Q Lorentzian); (3) the impulse-response shape — the gamma (gammatone) form or the rectangular-excitation (ROEX/Lorentzian) form; (4) the cascade order when realized as resonator sections. Persistence mechanism: it persists as a standard model of single-channel cochlear selectivity in the auditory-periphery literature (the gammatone and ROEX families; Moore's and Glasberg & Moore's auditory-filter work) and is the element from which filter banks are built. Boundary: it is a single analysis filter, not the array (filter-bank / mel-filterbank) that places many in parallel, and not the gammatone-filter alone — the gammatone-filter is the canonical resonator realization of this construct, so the two are distinct kinds, not the same thing. [formal: filtrum auditivum | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]
